topic: Which country has the most wild tigers? (India)
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

pib_2023_tigers.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India (MoEFCC / NTCA–WII)
pib_2023_tigers.title: All India Tiger Estimation 2022: Release of the detailed Report
pib_2023_tigers.notes: Status of Tigers 2022: average estimate 3,682 (upper limit 3,925), 6.1 %/yr growth; 'almost 75 % of the world's wild tigers'; Corbett highest reserve abundance (260)

pib_2026_tigers.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
pib_2026_tigers.title: India Leads the Wilderness in Tiger Conservation
pib_2026_tigers.notes: AITE 2022 = 3,682; 'more than doubled since 2006'; recent global estimates ≈ 5,711 wild tigers worldwide

wiki_tiger_reserves.title: Tiger reserves of India
wiki_tiger_reserves.notes: 58 tiger reserves as of 2025 (84,500 km²); 1,411 tigers in 2006 → 3,682 in 2022; about 70 % of the global wild population

wiki_tiger.title: Tiger
wiki_tiger.notes: global wild population 3,726–5,578 as of 2022 (IUCN); Endangered since 1986

wiki_siberian.title: Siberian tiger
wiki_siberian.notes: as of 2022 about 756 Siberian (Amur) tigers incl. 200 cubs in the Russian Far East; Sikhote-Alin, Primorsky Krai

wiki_corbett.title: Jim Corbett National Park
wiki_corbett.notes: 260 tigers in the 2022 census; India's first national park (1936), Uttarakhand

ht_2023.title: India's tiger count tops 3,600, Madhya Pradesh leads at 785

toi_2023.title: Pegged at 3,167 in April, India's tiger population now placed at 3,682
toi_2023.notes: 3,682 up from 2,967 in 2018; Corbett 260, Bandipur 150, Nagarhole 141; Sundarbans 101

claims.text: India has the most wild tigers: 3,682 (2022 All India Tiger Estimation average; range 3,167–3,925). With the global wild population put at 3,726–5,578 (IUCN 2022) or ≈ 5,711 (2026 estimate), India alone exceeds the rest of the world combined.

about thirty-seven hundred, more than the rest of the world combined

myths.myth: India has 75 % of the world's tigers.
myths.reality: That was the 2023 line against a ~4,500–5,000 global estimate; newer global figures (5,574–5,711) put India's share nearer two thirds — still more than the rest of the world combined.
The Sumatran tiger population is in the low hundreds; Russia's Amur tigers ≈ 750.

guardrails.why: Contested name — say 'the Gulf' or use both names (docs/BORDER_POLICY.md).
Sovereignty language on disputed areas is banned; say administers / claims.

landscape.our_gap: Feed versions put 'India' over a stock tiger. We count up the official 3,682 on the map, show where the reserves are and compare Russia's 750 honestly.
